Orientation

Describe a street

Use > for left → right, or < for right → left. Add measurements and check the preview.

Get the layout right

Use > for left → right or < for right → left: library > train > sidewalk > light rail. Commas or “and” also list features; “with” adds details. “Left of”, “right of” and “between” also work. Add widths and check the preview.

More wording examples
What can I describe?

Traffic: lane counts, one-way or two-way, northbound or southbound, turn pockets, bus lanes, tram tracks and bike paths.

Most accurate layout: list each feature in its exact order with > (left → right) or < (right → left). Example: library > train > 8 ft sidewalk > light rail. Use one direction throughout the chain. Keep a compound area in one step, such as “two lane road with a center turn lane” or “outdoor dining with a sidewalk”. Check the ordered preview and any notes before placing.

Other layouts: on the left, on the right, on both sides, named positions, or a list from left to right. Add explicit widths and lengths in feet, inches or metres for more predictable dimensions.

Places: houses, apartments, shops, restaurants, schools, offices, hospitals, parking lots, plazas, playgrounds and waterfronts.

Details: protected bike lanes, angled parking, rain gardens, trees, benches, lights, fountains, solar roofs and crossing styles. Use “no” or “without” to leave things out.

Activity and scenery: try “road with cars”, “bike path with cyclists”, “river with boats and kayaks”, or “beach with beach umbrellas and birds”. Select a surface to change its activity, use Add for scenery, or use Add item for individual items. Use Regenerate item positions to try a fresh arrangement.

Smarter reading with Claude (optional) · Not set up

The built-in reader works offline for most descriptions. With your own key, Ask Claude helps interpret more detailed wording. The key stays in this browser, and requests go straight from here to Anthropic. API usage is billed by Anthropic.
